title: Federal Wage & Hour Complaint (FLSA)
description: Step-by-step guide for filing a federal wage and hour complaint under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for unpaid wages, overtime violations, or minimum wage violations.

steps.title: Determine if the FLSA covers your situation
steps.description: The FLSA covers most private and public sector employees, but there are exemptions. Confirm coverage before proceeding.
actions: Confirm your employer is covered: businesses with $500,000+ annual revenue, or engaged in interstate commerce
Confirm you are a non-exempt employee (not executive, administrative, professional, or outside sales exempt)
Identify the violation type: unpaid minimum wage, unpaid overtime (>40hrs/week), off-the-clock work, illegal deductions
Calculate the amount owed: overtime = 1.5x regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek
Check if your state has stronger protections (California, New York often do — consider state filing too)

deadlines.notes: FLSA statute of limitations: 2 years for non-willful violations, 3 years for willful violations. Time starts from each missed paycheck.

steps.agency: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division (WHD)

steps.title: Gather evidence and calculate damages
steps.description: Strong documentation is essential. Collect everything you have and reconstruct what you don't.
actions: Collect all pay stubs, pay statements, and W-2/1099 forms
Gather time records: punch cards, timesheets, app records, email or phone logs showing hours worked
Document any off-the-clock work with dates, times, and witnesses
Calculate total unpaid wages: regular pay + 1.5x overtime rate for each affected workweek
Note: FLSA allows liquidated damages (double the unpaid wages) plus attorney fees
Keep a written log of any communications with your employer about pay issues

deadlines.notes: Collect records as far back as 3 years for willful violations.

steps.title: File a complaint with the Wage and Hour Division
steps.description: The WHD investigates FLSA complaints for free. You do not need an attorney to file. Filing is confidential and retaliation is illegal.
actions: File online at dol.gov/agencies/whd/contact/complaints or call 1-866-487-9243
Provide: employer name and address, your job title, dates of employment, approximate hours worked, pay rate, and description of violation
The WHD will determine whether to investigate — investigations can take months
You will NOT be identified to your employer without your consent during investigation
Retaliation for filing a complaint is illegal under FLSA Section 15(a)(3)
Keep a copy of your complaint confirmation number

deadlines.notes: File as soon as possible. Each paycheck missed starts its own limitations clock.

steps.agency: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division

steps.title: Alternatively or additionally: file a private lawsuit
steps.description: You can file your own lawsuit in federal or state court without going through the WHD. This may be faster and allows you to control the case.
actions: Consult an employment attorney — most take FLSA cases on contingency (no upfront cost)
You can file in federal district court or state court with federal jurisdiction
FLSA allows recovery of: unpaid wages, equal amount as liquidated damages, and attorney fees
Filing a WHD complaint does NOT prevent you from filing a lawsuit (you can do both)
If WHD recovers wages on your behalf, you cannot also sue for the same wages
Class or collective actions possible if other employees were similarly affected

deadlines.notes: For collective actions, each individual must 'opt in' — statute of limitations tolled only upon filing consent.

steps.title: Cooperate with WHD investigation or litigation
steps.description: Whether through a WHD investigation or private lawsuit, you will need to provide information and documentation.
actions: Respond promptly to all WHD investigator requests for information
Do not destroy or alter any records — this can hurt your case
Provide a written statement if requested
If in litigation: participate in discovery, provide documents, and attend depositions
Continue documenting any ongoing violations or retaliation
Communicate regularly with your attorney if you have one

deadlines.notes: WHD investigations typically conclude within 6-12 months. Litigation timelines vary.

steps.title: Receive resolution — back pay, settlement, or judgment
steps.description: WHD investigations may result in a compliance agreement and back pay. Lawsuits may settle or go to trial.
actions: WHD resolution: you receive back wages + possibly liquidated damages collected by the agency
Private settlement: review carefully with an attorney before signing any release of claims
Judgment: if you win at trial, court will award back pay, liquidated damages, and attorney fees
Review any settlement agreement for scope — ensure it does not waive future claims
Report settlement income to the IRS (back wages are taxable; liquidated damages may be too)
Keep all records of the resolution permanently

deadlines.notes: Do not sign any settlement releasing claims without reviewing with an attorney.
